1.explanation:
1. lighthouse-core/computed/trace-of-tab.js is where Lighthouse inspects the raw DevTools trace and throws LHError.errors.NO_FCP as soon as it sees no firstContentfulPaint event. Since background tabs don’t fire paint events, this code will always reject. 
2. clients/devtools-entry.js is the entry point that builds the extension’s runtime config. It currently doesn’t force real-time DevTools throttling, so background tabs won’t emit FCP. By adding settings.throttlingMethod = 'devtools' (and/or using the perf-config approach) in createConfig, the extension will run against the real timeline in DevTools—allowing FCP to be recorded in hidden tabs and preventing trace-of-tab.js from throwing NO_FCP.
1.bug_scenario: When Lighthouse is run as a Chrome extension against a page that’s loaded in a background tab, the DevTools trace never emits a “firstContentfulPaint” event. As a result, the computed artifact in trace-of-tab.js throws the NO_FCP error and every performance metric in the extension UI shows “Error!” with NO_FCP.
